summary: This defines a Cookie class: a blueprint that stores one cookie's flavor and can describe itself in a sentence. It is the starting point for a small bakery program built up over the next few exercises.

lines.text: Declares the class, which acts as the blueprint for every individual cookie object the bakery program will create.
Each cookie carries its own flavor. `private` keeps it hidden from outside code, and `final` means it is set once when the cookie is made and never changes afterwards.
The constructor is the special method that runs when you write `new Cookie(...)`; it demands a flavor so no cookie can exist without one.
Assigns the value passed in to the object's own field. The `this.` prefix distinguishes the field from the parameter, which shares the same name.
A behaviour that belongs to the cookie itself: rather than another class reaching in for the flavor, the cookie reports on itself.
Builds the sentence by joining text with the field's value and hands it back to the caller, which is free to print it, store it, or display it.
